<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The browser MCP server failed to register.

I'll fetch the API directly to inspect timetable data and league counts. Real data will strengthen layout recommendations. I'm also checking whether "foldable entry" refers to Club300's pattern.

I'll check for an existing bulk timetable endpoint. The data model needs per-league weeks with date, venue, and status, aggregated across the selected leagues. This is essentially a calendar resource-scheduling problem. I need to design a layout that makes simultaneous dates and venues obvious at a glance.

Three layout options are under consideration. A date-by-league matrix would show same-date collisions clearly. An agenda grouped by date would be easy to scan. A venue-by-date matrix would emphasize venue sharing.

A league-by-date matrix would let users see both their own schedule and cross-league collisions. Matchday numbers would misalign across different calendars, so actual dates should be used as columns. A calendar-month grid is another option being considered.

The calendar-month grid would display league and venue as colored chips. Multiple events on the same day would stack vertically. A shared venue could use a common color. This suits sparse bowling schedules well. The main goal is identifying which bowling center hosts which league on which weekend. In Bavaria, several leagues often play on the same weekends at different centers. Some leagues may even share a single center.

The preferred layout is a date-grouped agenda with venue clustering. Leagues sharing the same center on the same day would appear together under that venue. This makes simultaneous dates and venues obvious at a glance.

A league-by-date matrix would complement the agenda view. Matching cells in the same column indicate overlapping dates, while identical venue text shows shared houses. For the myClub filter, which typically covers one to three leagues, a dense matrix would be overkill; the agenda view remains preferable.

A full season can contain twenty or more leagues. That makes a matrix too wide and an agenda too long. Real data will reveal league counts and date alignment. Venue uniqueness and date formats still need verification.

$events = @()

**Recommendation:** a **date-first Spielplan**, nested by venue, as one foldable on the season page (`/liga?season=11/12`, no league). Same Sunday and same house then sit in one block — no scanning across 27 tables.

I treated the A N1 Termine card as the **data source**, not the page that gets the new section. If you instead want Spielplan on the single-league page, say so.

---

### What the data actually looks like (11/12)

- **27 leagues**, **6–8 Spieltage** each, almost all on **Sundays**.
- About **17 distinct dates**. A typical Sunday has **6–13 leagues**.
- **Same house on the same day** happens regularly (always 2 leagues in this season), e.g. Brunnthal: BL S1 + KL S3 on 18.09.2011.
- Termine already has everything we need per league: **Spieltag, Datum, Ort** (`/league/get_season_timetable`). There is **no clock time** — “same time” means the same calendar day.
- Venue strings are messy (`Isar München` vs `Isar-München`, `Dream-Bowl` vs `Dream-Bowl München`). Collision grouping should normalize those later.

Stacked Termine tables (one per league) would **not** make overlaps obvious. A week-number matrix would also miss them: Spieltag 1 of BayL is not the same Sunday as Spieltag 1 of A N1.

---

### Proposed layout (collision-first)

One `CollapsibleSection` **Spielplan**, above the standings, **open by default** (the page is already long; you can collapse it).

```
So 18.09.2011 · 13 Ligen · 11 Orte
  Brunnthal                    2 Ligen
    BL S1 · Spieltag 1
    KL S3 · Spieltag 1
  Extreme Dettelbach           2 Ligen
    BL N2 · Spieltag 1
    BZL N2 · Spieltag 1
  BluBowl Nürnberg
    A N2 · Spieltag 1
  …
```

Reading order is **when → where → which league**. Shared houses are stacked and marked; a Sunday with 13 leagues is one block, not 13 rows in different tables.

- Date header: weekday + date + counts.
- Venue with 2+ leagues: compact “2 Ligen” mark (and a light surface tint).
- League chip: short name (`A N1`), long name on hover, Spieltag number (BayL ST1 ≠ A N1 ST1).
- Chip links to that matchday (`/liga?season=…&league=…&week=…`).
- Dates missing/TBD: last bucket **Ohne Datum**.

**Mein Club:** same view, leagues already in the season filter (`filteredLeagues`). With 2–3 club leagues it becomes a travel calendar. No extra myClub logic beyond that.

---

### What I would not use as the main view

| Approach | Why not as default |
|---|---|
| Liga × Datum matrix | 27 × 17 is dense; venue names overflow; mobile needs horizontal scroll; same-house still needs extra highlighting |
| Month calendar | ~17 Sundays over 6 months — mostly empty cells |
| One Termine table per league | Current data, but collisions are invisible |

A **Nach Liga** toggle (each league as a row of dates/venues, like stacked Termine) is useful as a **second mode**, not the default. Your stated job is “same day, same house, at a glance.”

---

### Placement and scope

| Filter | Spielplan shows |
|---|---|
| Season only | All leagues that season |
| Season + Mein Club | That club’s leagues only |
| Season + league | Keep the existing Termine card; no second Spielplan |

---

Three choices before implementation:

1. **Default = date → venue → league** as above, with optional **Nach Liga** toggle?
2. Spielplan **open by default**, above the standings?
3. Confirm it lives on **season-only** `/liga?season=…`, not on `/liga?season=…&league=A+N1`?

Once those are set, implementation can reuse `get_season_timetable` per league in scope (cached; ~27 calls unfiltered, 1–3 with Mein Club). A bulk endpoint can wait.

---

_**User**_

1. lets go with that default
2. make it open as of now, we might change that later
3. confirmed! only season view, evnetually filtered by myClub

---

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Checking how DataTable maps columns from nested groups to ensure correct TableData parsing.

Flask TableData wraps columns in ColumnGroup objects. The parser will flatten these groups and map array rows by index to fields. It will handle both array and object row formats.

Venue keys will be normalized by NFC-decomposition, trimming, lowercasing, and replacing separators with spaces. This merges variants like "Isar München" and "Isar-München" while keeping distinct names separate. Display names will be chosen from the longest or most frequent original string per group.

Dates will be sorted with valid ISO strings first, followed by TBD, NaN, and empty values in an undated bucket. Weekdays will display in German short form using UTC dates to prevent timezone shifts. Leagues within a venue will sort alphabetically by short name. Venues within a date will sort by league count with collisions on top, then alphabetically.

Dates will sort chronologically. The component will accept a LeagueOption[] array from filteredLeagues. While the leagues query is still loading, a skeleton state will appear. When myClub is active but participation data is still loading, filteredLeagues may be empty or incomplete.

The existing pattern returns all leagues while participation data loads, which risks a flash of 27 timetable fetches before filtering down to 2-3. I will instead wait until the leagues are fully ready before fetching timetables, either by passing a `leaguesReady` flag or only supplying the league list once loading finishes.

useSeasonTimetables will wrap useQueries and accept an enabled flag. Fetching will only proceed once leagues are loaded and at least one league is selected. Each league gets its own query key scoped to season and league.

The hook uses fetchJson to call /league/get_season_timetable with season and league parameters. Each query is gated by enabled, season, and league presence. Navigation links will use useAppLink to preserve myClub across seasons and leagues.

Noticed that buildLeagueNavPath drops myClub because it rebuilds URLSearchParams without preserving global search params. I will use useAppLink or linkForPath instead. Now drafting the SeasonSpielplan component signature.

The component now consumes translations and navigation helpers. It passes the season and mapped league IDs into the timetable hook, gating fetches until the league list finishes loading. Pending and error states are tracked across all league queries. Results are fed into a memoized planner that groups events by date and venue. The UI renders inside a CollapsibleSection titled "Spielplan" that defaults to open.

The collapsible section will use "Spielplan" as its title. A subtitle in the body will show the season and league count, such as "11/12 · 27 Ligen".

The collapsible section will use only a title with no eyebrow, matching patterns like "Besondere Momente". An optional caption inside the body will explain grouping by date and venue. Copy stays short.

The layout uses a vertical stack of day sections. Each day header shows the German weekday and date, plus a muted caption counting leagues and venues. Inside, venues are rendered as bordered rounded cards.

Shared venues get accent borders and tinted backgrounds. Each card shows the venue name and a label counting its leagues. A wrapped list of league links follows below.

Each league link shows the short name and a mono-styled week number. Shared venues use the same accent border and tinted background as tournament winner cards for an at-a-glance signal.

Chips will use small rounded labels with border and surface backgrounds, switching to accent styling on hover. Shared venue chips will sit on the tinted background. Date headers will pair the German weekday in normal text with the numeric date in mono. An undated section will appear at the end. Empty states will show no timetables. Errors will be shown alongside successful leagues.

League chips will use short_name, with long_name shown in tooltips. Missing LeagueOptions fall back to the raw league value. The browser fetches the Flask-wrapped JSON directly, so the parser will flatten the nested columns and map array rows by index.

PowerShell may stringify TableData unexpectedly, though Flask JSON should be fine. TBD dates and week numbers may arrive as strings or numbers. Tests will cover date-and-venue grouping, venue normalization, TBD buckets, shared-venue flags, sorting, array and object row extraction, and empty-table handling. German fallbacks will be used for i18n.

Adding `ui.league.spielplan_*` translation keys to `i18n_service.py` for consistency with recent frontend additions. Checking existing `ui.league` clusters in that file to follow established patterns.
</details></think>

The rainbowPastel palette contains only ten colors. That may be too few for many leagues.

RainbowPastel and harmonic10 will be concatenated to provide enough distinct colors for roughly twenty venues. Leagues will be ordered by strength, with the highest level at the top of the inverted y-axis.

Date labels will be short categories such as "18.09" or "So 18.09". This keeps same-day events vertically aligned without clustering issues.

Tooltip will display the full date. Each point will carry its abbreviated league name inside a small rounded rectangle symbol. The chart may feel dense with twenty-seven leagues and eight dates, so abbreviations will be kept minimal.

Text color will be computed dynamically against each pastel background to prevent contrast issues. An optional click callback will be added to the EChart wrapper. A data zoom slider is also being considered for the long timeline.

The chart will need roughly 800 pixels of height to fit all 27 leagues. The left margin must accommodate long venue names. A scrollable bottom legend will display full venue names. The implementation will start with an abbreviation helper and a function to collect events from the parsed timetable.

The chart will replace the day-block layout entirely. Undated events will appear as a small note beneath the graph. A new `buildSpielplanChart` function will generate the chart model from leagues, tables, and language. Tests will cover abbreviation logic and the chart model. Hint text and i18n keys will be updated accordingly.

Leagues will be sorted by level first, then by German short name. Venues will be assigned colors by sorting their display names and cycling through the palette. The abbreviation algorithm strips filler words, which risks collapsing names like "OK Bowling Bindlach" into a single letter.

A tokenization helper splits venue names at camelCase boundaries and whitespace. Initials are drawn from tokens longer than one character, or from single-character tokens if no longer ones exist. This prevents collapsing names like "OK Bowling Bindlach" into a single letter.

CamelCase splitting is needed to turn "Dreambowl" into "Dream Bowl" so it abbreviates to DBM rather than DM. Prefix-based splitting is fragile. Collision resolution will try initials first.

The abbreviation helper now tries several candidate forms. It starts with initials. Then it uses the first two letters of the first token plus the first letter of the remaining tokens. Finally it builds a four-letter code from the first two letters of every token. It selects the first unused candidate. Incremental suffixes like DBM2 are avoided.

Umlauts will be stripped from venue names during abbreviation generation. Click events will pass the league and week data. Y-axis labels will use monospaced fonts. Axis label colors will be read from CSS variables to support dark mode.

A `chartInk()` helper will read CSS custom properties from the root element. It extracts foreground, muted, border, and surface colors. ECharts canvas does not support CSS variables directly. The helper falls back to `#18181b` if a property is missing.

The CSS variable `--color-foreground` is merely an alias for `--ds-foreground`, so the chart ink helper must target `--ds-foreground` directly. ECharts HTML tooltips will be used to display the full date, location, and present leagues for each point.

Each scatter point will carry its date key, venue, and list of present leagues. Tooltip content will group all events on that date by venue. A faint line series was considered to trace each league’s season path, but ECharts lines cannot easily change color per venue, so that idea is set aside.

Y-axis splitLines will serve as the faint league tracks instead of separate line series. Each colored dot will sit on its own grid row. Symbols will be small rounded rectangles with the abbreviated league name inside. Chart height will scale with league count, plus a fixed bottom margin for the legend. The grid will use tight margins and `containLabel: true`. Undated events will be listed separately below the chart.

The hint text will read: "Eine Zeile je Liga, Farbe = Halle. Gleiche Spalte = gleicher Tag." New i18n keys will be added for it.

`collectSpielplanEvents` will be exported to avoid duplicating event collection logic elsewhere.

The chart model and option builder will move into dedicated frontend files. `seasonSpielplan.ts` will hold the abbreviation helper, event collector, and chart model types. `frontend/src/lib/spielplanChart.ts` will contain the ECharts option builder to keep the data library free of chart dependencies.

The ECharts click handler will be bound via a useEffect hook that removes the previous listener and adds the new one whenever the callback changes. The callback must be wrapped in useCallback to keep its identity stable. The SeasonSpielplan component will compute the chart model inside a useMemo hook that depends on the leagues, query results, and language.

The click handler will call `useNavigate` to jump to the linked league page. A fallback HTML legend below the chart is being considered in case the ECharts scroll legend feels cramped. The abbreviation helper will be tested against specific venue names like Dream-Bowl München and BluBowl Nürnberg.

Venue abbreviations will be three letters, such as BRU for Brunnthal and IM for Isar München. City-Augsburg and City Augsburg share one venue key, so they collapse into a single legend entry. The collectSpielplanEvents helper will iterate over the leagues array and gather events from each table.

The chart model types are defined. `SpielplanChartModel` holds the inverted league list, chronological dates, venue legends with colors, and the scatter points.

The chart model will store events grouped by date in a Map. Category axes will use date labels and league short names for robustness. The y-axis will invert so the top league appears first. Venue colors will cycle through a 20-color pastel palette and wrap around if more venues exist.

The color palette will combine both the rainbowPastel and harmonic10 sets to keep venue colors distinct. Labels will switch between white and dark gray based on the background color’s perceived brightness.

Tooltip styling will use ECharts extraCssText to create a stadium-like appearance. Click events will be restricted to the scatter series. Each venue gets its own scatter series with a roundRect symbol sized 42 by 22 pixels. The encode mapping will assign the first axis to date labels and the second to league short names. Item borders will be removed and the fill color will match the venue color.

Each dot will show its abbreviation in a small monospaced font. Hovering scales the dot by 15 percent. Legend entries will pair abbreviations with full names. The bottom grid margin will be 96 pixels to fit the legend. With 27 series the legend will scroll with page icons. The old SpielplanDayBlock component will be removed. The chart will use collectSpielplanEvents directly.

`buildSeasonSpielplan` will stay for test coverage and tooltip data. Date labels will be short like `18.09` to save space; the tooltip will show the full date including year. The chart model will be built by combining `collectSpielplanEvents` with venue grouping. Clicked points will navigate to the linked league page using the league identifier and week number.

The ECharts click effect must not dispose the chart instance. The collapsible section will stay mounted by default because it is already open, so no lazy mount is required. A ResizeObserver will handle recalculation when the panel is reopened.

Gridlines will mark each date and league row. Symbol sizes will be 46 by 20 pixels, widening slightly for four-letter abbreviations. The abbreviation tokenizer will split on hyphens and camelCase boundaries, keeping only tokens of at least two characters.

Abbreviation rules are now fixed. Tokens are split on hyphens and camelCase boundaries, then joined into initials. Filler words like arena or center are kept. Every abbreviation is capped at four letters. Examples include DBPU for Dream Bowl Palace Unt fö, CAN for Cosmos Nürnberg, and OBB for OK Bindlach.

Tests will be written for the chart model and abbreviation helper. The tooltip formatter will receive the event map, date format, and translation strings for labels like "Spieltag" and "Ligen". The club300 ECharts implementation will be reviewed as a visual reference.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The boxy polygonal appearance comes from `roundRect` using `r = Math.min(w, h) / 4`, which caps the corner radius too aggressively.

A custom SVG path with half-height radius is the correct pill shape. ECharts roundRect cannot accept a custom radius, so the custom path is the only viable approach. I will compact the path for robustness and retry the browser test before shipping.

Comma-separated coordinates are needed for the SVG arc flags to parse correctly.
</details></think>

Selecting the "all" season currently shows nothing when no league is chosen, because the overview view requires a specific league.

The all-seasons view will remain empty when no league is selected, even if a region is chosen. New i18n keys will be added near the Spielplan section. The `leagueSelect.ts` module will import from `leagueLevel.ts` rather than duplicating the ID map. Frontend tests will be written before implementation begins.

The dropdown will receive the complete `myClub`-filtered league list plus the current division and league, letting it compute the visible subset internally.

A new `getLeagueDivision` helper will be added alongside `getLeagueLevel` to map each league ID to its division. Unknown-level leagues will be grouped under the label "Weitere Ligen". The next step is to review existing frontend test patterns and locate the correct i18n insertion point.

Updating sanitization effects, league selection logic, allowed leagues for standings, and FilterBar props to support filtering by section headers.

Adding level validation to the sanitizer. It now strips invalid level parameters when no matching leagues exist. Region and level checks must run independently rather than in a sequential else-if chain.

The sanitizer now validates region and level separately. It strips invalid division parameters when no matching leagues exist in the selected region. It also removes invalid level parameters when no matching leagues satisfy both the level and region constraints.

Simplifying the sanitizer logic. After the season and league blocks, it extracts the effective region and level from the remaining query parameters. It then checks whether a league is still active while region or level filters remain, and validates those against the allowed leagues list.

Replacing the existing `else if (region)` sanitizer block entirely. The always-on sanitizer now strips division and level parameters whenever a league is selected. When no league is active, it removes invalid divisions and invalid levels.

The always-on sanitizer now also strips invalid level parameters when no matching leagues satisfy both the level and region constraints. It applies these changes via `setSearchParams` with `{ replace: true }` whenever any parameter is removed.

Implementing the `onLeagueSelect` handler. It clears the league parameter and resets week, team, and round filters. Selecting a full league sets the league value and removes both division and level. Selecting a division sets the division value and removes level.

Finishing the `onLeagueSelect` handler. It now falls back to setting a level parameter when no league or division is selected, otherwise clearing both division and level. The `allowedLeaguesForStandings` helper returns null when a full league is active, and returns scoped leagues when a region or level filter is present. The FilterBar component receives the `level` prop. The season change handler preserves the level parameter instead of dropping it.

_**Agent (grok-4.6)**_

The club page URLs are fine. The team APIs were failing because of the **season format on the wire**.

The React app sends `season=25-26` (dash) so a reverse proxy does not treat `25/26` as a path. Liga and Spieler routes already convert that back to `25/26`. **Team routes did not**, so they looked up the literal key `"25-26"` in history that is keyed `"25/26"`.

Against the running server that produced:

| Request | `season=25-26` (what the page sends) | `season=25/26` |
|---|---|---|
| `/team/get_consistency_metrics` | **400** “Team … not found in season 25-26” | 200 with metrics |
| `/team/get_special_matches` | 200 **empty `{}`** | 200 with highs/lows |
| `/team/get_clutch_analysis` | 200 `{"error":"No team data found"}` | 200 with clutch stats |

`/team/get_available_seasons`, `/team/get_team_history`, and `/team/get_league_comparison` never take a season query, so they already succeeded (history ~10s, league comparison ~20s).

I added the same `normalize_season_query_value` helper on the team routes (`25-26` → `25/26`) and covered it with tests (`5 passed`). Flask is started outside this session and has **not** reloaded yet — the live `:5000` process still returns the old 400/empty responses. Restart the backend (`start.sh`) and both URLs should load the Mannschaft blocks for 25/26.
